policy.snapshot_rule: Every capture keeps its raw SHA-256 and the clock time it was read. A capture is never edited; a correction is a new capture.
policy.delta_rule: The site publishes the change between two captures, never a single level presented as though it were stable.
policy.not_listed_rule: Absence from the report means the league did not list the player. It is never rendered as 'healthy' or 'available'.
policy.honest_limitation: The brief asks for at least daily capture of the official report, club depth pages and inactive lists. This repository holds the captures listed below and no others. It cannot self-schedule; a scheduled job must own the cadence. Until that job exists, the number of vintages is what you see, not what was asked for.

capture_quality_findings.why_it_matters: A team whose entire block carries no game status and no non-participation practice flag is indistinguishable from 'everyone practised fully'. Any model that reads a blank cell as healthy will under-estimate that team's unavailability by exactly this many players.
two_possible_causes: the league had not yet published game statuses for that team when the capture was taken
the capture omitted the column values for that block
capture_quality_findings.how_to_resolve: Take a third capture of the same week. If the block is populated, the first capture was a reading artefact; if it is still blank, the league had not published. Held open as an irregularity until that capture exists.

designation_reliability.note: This is the empirical answer to 'what does Questionable mean'. It replaces any borrowed percentage, and it carries n and a Wilson interval because a play rate without its sample size is not evidence.
designation_reliability.caveat: A snap-count row proves participation, not a start, and it does not prove the player was on the game-day 48. It is the strongest join the committed data supports, and it is labelled as a participation join.
